**My reasoning:**

I've been farming this land since I was young. My family has about 10 mu here in Quzhou. There's really only one way to farm around here — winter wheat, then summer maize on the same land. That's what my father did, what my neighbors do, and what gets grain on the table and some cash at harvest. I'm not going to try anything new at my age. The wheat-maize rotation fills the whole year and uses the land properly.

For wheat, I'll buy the improved seed from the township supply station — probably Jimai 22 or whatever variety the station recommends this year. For maize, I always use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335. The hybrid maize yields are much better. I've seen that over the years.

On fertilizer, I put down phosphate compound fertilizer at planting as base, then top-dress urea in spring for wheat or after seedling establishment for maize. I know some people say we overuse fertilizer, but I don't want to risk a poor harvest. I'll do what I always do.

Wheat needs three irrigations here: the freeze water in November to protect roots, jointing in March, and heading in May. Maize needs at least two — one after sowing if it's dry, and one around tasseling. The groundwater pump hasn't failed me yet.

I spray herbicide for both crops, and for wheat I also spray fungicide twice against rust and powdery mildew — that's been a problem some years. Maize gets herbicide plus one insecticide spray if the fall armyworm shows up.

Rotary tillage both times — it's faster and the machine is easy to hire.
